record.original_question: Does the three-dimensional Euler equation have wandering solutions, analogous to Nadirashvili's two-dimensional annulus example in which a neighborhood of an initial condition never returns sufficiently close after some time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on a bounded three-dimensional domain $M\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ (for instance, a solid torus or a spherical shell) with smooth boundary, written for the velocity field $u:M\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^3$ as
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p,\qquad \mathrm{div}\,u=0,\qquad u\cdot n|_{\partial M}=0.$$
Regard the Euler flow as a dynamical system on a suitable space $\mathcal{V}$ of divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$, equipped with a fixed topology (e.g., $C^k$ for some $k\geq 1$, or $L^2$). Call a solution $u(t)$ \emph{wandering} if there exists an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathcal{V}$ of the initial datum $u(0)$ and a time $T>0$ such that the time-$t$ Euler flow $\Phi_t(U)$ satisfies $\Phi_t(U)\cap U=\emptyset$ for all $t\geq T$.

In dimension two on an annulus, Nadirashvili constructed such wandering solutions: there exist smooth, divergence-free initial velocity fields together with a $C^1$-open neighborhood that, after some positive time, never returns to itself under the 2D Euler flow.

Question: Do wandering solutions, in the above sense, exist for the three-dimensional Euler equations on some bounded smooth domain $M\subset\mathbb{R}^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: Nadirashvili's 1991 result establishes wandering solutions for the 2D Euler equation on an annulus. According to current literature on geometric hydrodynamics, the existence of a 3D analogue remains unknown; related progress uses KAM-type methods and stability/instability of steady states, but no full 3D wandering construction has been verified.

status_evidence.title: Wandering solutions of Euler's D-2 equation
status_evidence.snippet: Nadirashvili (1991) constructed wandering solutions of the 2D Euler equation on an annulus.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the 2D wandering result that the 3D problem seeks to extend.

status_evidence.title: KAM theory and the 3D Euler equation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies non-mixing and KAM-type behavior for 3D Euler; a 3D analogue of Nadirashvili's wandering result is noted as unknown.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the 3D version of Nadirashvili's wandering theorem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the existence of wandering solutions for 3D Euler as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is presented as open in the geometric hydrodynamics open-problem collection.
